The present revision has been preferred by the petitioner,
aggrieved by the order dated 26.04.2000 passed by the appellate court, the court of II Additional Sessions Judge, Raisen in Criminal Appeal No. 119/99 Padam Singh Vs. State of M.P. whereby learned Additional Sessions Judge has maintained sentence passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Raisen in Criminal Case No. 1208/1993, convicting the petitioner under section 7(1)read with 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred as "the Act").
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner has taken a very short ground to state that the right of the petitioner under Section 13(2) of the Act was not complied with.

3. The brief facts essential to appreciate the case against the petitioner is that a complaint was instituted by the complainant K.L. Jaiswal Food Inspector, in which it was stated that on 28/08/1993 at about 9 O'clock, the complainant had gone to bus stand, Obedullaganj to check the quality of food material.
The petitioner herein said to have found carrying 2 Kgs. of mixed milk.

On doubt that the petitioner may carry adulterated milk, the complainant introduced himself and Padam Singh vs The State Of M.P. on 22 May, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105590948/
1 insisted to take the sample of the said milk.

sentences.text: A notice form-6 was given to the petitioner and upon the consent of the petitioner 750ml milk was purchased as sample.
After following due procedure, the milk was sent to the Public Analyst and the report of public analyst revealed that the milk was adulterated.
The complaint was filed by the Food Inspector as mentioned hereinabove and the trial court convicted the petitioner for the said offence.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn the attention of this Court to paragraph No. 10 of the appellate court's order in which learned counsel for the appellant/ petitioner had placed before the appellate court the judgment of this Court in Food Inspector Balaghat Vs. Tejlal 1995 Cr. L.R. (M.P.) 95 in which this court was pleased to acquit the petitioner in that case, this court arrived at the finding that Criminal Revision No. 605/2000.
the mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the Act was not fulfilled.

entities.text: Food Inspector Balaghat Vs. Tejlal 1995 Cr. L.R. (M.P.) 95
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Court observed that the notice under Section 13(2) of the Act along with report of Public Analyst which was alleged to have been sent to the petitioner in that case was not proved, as prosecution failed to place on record either the receipt of the registered post by which the said notice and the report was dispatched or the acknowledgment with the said notice and report were received by the accused.
4.

Learned appellate court however, dismissed the appeal filed by the petitioner herein by distinguishing on facts from the case placed before it on the ground that in this case, the prosecution was able to prove the receipt of dispatch of the said notice of the food inspector.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has thereafter argued that even before the trial court,
consistent stand of the petitioner herein was that he did not receive notice or public analyst report as mandatory under Section 13(2) of the Act.

However, on going through the record of the case and as was fairly stated by the learned counsel for the petitioner himself, Ex. P/14 before the trial court is a copy of the receipt of dispatch of the registered post allegedly containing notice and report of Public Analyst to the petitioner.
The name of the petitioner is shown in the place where it is given a address.

However, in order to put the said Ex. P/14 under doubt learned Criminal Revision No.

counsel for the petitioner has drawn the attention of this court to the deposition of PW/1 recorded before the learned trial court.
PW/1 is the complainant who, at the relevant point of time, was on the post of Sanitary Inspector with the State Health Department.

In paragraph 5 of the cross-examination, this witness states that " ;g dguk xyr gS fd vkjksih ?kVuk fnukad dks nw? k cspus ugha vk;k FkkA ?kVuk fnukad dks vdsys vfHk;qDr dk gh lSEiy fy;k FkkA ;g dguk xyr gS fd vkjksih dks /kkjk & 13(2)

It is admitted by the complainant itself that the receipt of dispatch of notice and publi analyst report has not been filed by the complainant.
Under the circumstances Ex. P/14 is called into doubt, as it is the admitted position that the complainant himself has stated that the said receipt was not filed.
Even otherwise Ex. P/14 appears to be photocopy of the original receipt, which does not bear the endorsement of the trial court on the said exhibit that the original has been seen.
Under the circumstances, the inability of the prosecution to establish the dispatch of the notice under Section 13(1) of the Act to raises a doubt in favour of the accused.
